text: 9,000 bytes of repeated English compressed to 108, far below what its per-character entropy of 4.40 predicts. Why?
choices: Per-character entropy overestimates whenever the alphabet is smaller than 256 symbols.
The source coding theorem applies only to random sources, not to natural language.
gzip applies Huffman coding twice, which halves the entropy bound each pass.
The text was one sentence repeated, and LZ77 found the repetition — which per-character entropy cannot see, since it looks at one character at a time.
explanation: It is conditional entropy again: with context, the real entropy of that particular source is near zero. The random-letters row behaved as predicted — entropy 4.70, compressed to 62.6%, close to 4.70/8 = 58.75% — because there was no structure beyond the fact that only 26 of 256 byte values occurred, and gzip extracted approximately that and nothing more.
